basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 43.' and it opens '(Vers. 43.) Et clamavit ante eum praeco, et constituit eum super omnem terram Aegypti.'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 43.) Et clamavit ante eum praeco, et constituit eum super omnem terram Aegypti. Pro quo Aquila transtulit: Et clamavit in conspectu ejus adgeniculationem. Symmachus ipsum Hebraicum sermonem interpretans ait: Et clamavit ante eum ABRECH (אברך). Unde mihi videtur non tam praeco, sive adgeniculatio, quae in salutando vel adorando Joseph accipi potest, intelligenda: quam illud quod Hebraei tradunt, dicentes patrem tenerum, et hoc sermone transferri; AB (אב) quippe dicitur pater, RECH (רך) delicatus sive tenerrimus; significante Scriptura, quod juxta prudentiam quidem pater omnium fuerit: sed juxta aetatem tenerrimus adolescens et puer.
